pinboard.description:
“Shane,” he says, dread filling his stomach, “is this Boston Lily’s house?”

“Maybe,” Shane says, dropping down another cooler with a loud bang. “But shhhhh,” he says, putting a finger to his lips, “you can’t tell, okay?”

“Shane,” Hayden says, a little desperately. “Shane, we have to go.”

“No,” Shane says, drunk and stubborn and pushing the doorbell about fifty thousand times in quick succession until Hayden pulls his arm away.

“Shane,” Hayden says, nearly a plea, “listen, I know she broke your heart, but dropping off two hundred pounds of tuna isn’t-”

Before he can finish telling Shane that a drive-by tuna fishing isn’t a cure for a broken heart, the door opens. When it does, though, it’s not some buxom Boston beauty in a silky negligee.

It’s Ilya fucking Rozanov.

Hayden’s one consolation in this mindfuck is that at least Rozanov looks equally surprised at finding himself in this situation.

pinboard.description:
“And what about the others?” Crowell stops mid-sentence, his mouth hanging open. “The others?” Shane can see Ilya in his periphery, can imagine the shock on his face as he snaps it in Shane’s direction, but he ignores it. He’s starting to realize the enormity of what he’s about to say, but adrenaline is outweighing fear. It isn’t Shane’s decision-making brain in charge right now, it’s his hockey brain, and he can see the play without having to think about it, his body moving on instinct. “The others,” he says again. “If you’re going to bench me and Rozanov, what about all the other players I’ve had sex with?”
In a moment of panic and fury over Crowell benching him and Ilya, Shane impulsively decides to tell him that he’s slept with other hockey players too. Little does he know what he's created. (Words: 8,329)
